audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Leviticus / Vayiqra lamp, bread, blasphemy-case, and proportional-justice text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for continual lamp, bread of presence, blasphemy case, equal law for native and sojourner, animal restitution, and lex talionis/proportional justice. Strong anti-violence and anti-vigilantism safeguards required.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

familiar.text: Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually.

verses.restored: Outside veil of testimony, in tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before YHWH continually; age-long statute throughout your generations.

familiar.text: Without the vail of the testimony, in the tabernacle of the congregation, shall Aaron order it from the evening unto the morning before the LORD continually: it shall be a statute for ever in your generations.

familiar.text: Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.

verses.restored: It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in holy place, for Holy of Holies it is to him from fire-offerings of YHWH, age-long due.

familiar.text: And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; and they shall eat it in the holy place: for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the LORD made by fire by a perpetual statute.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

familiar.text: Bring forth him that hath cursed without the camp; and let all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let all the congregation stone him.

verses.restored: To children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Any man who curses his Divine shall bear his sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin.

verses.restored: The one who blasphemes/pierces name YHWH shall surely be put to death; all congregation shall surely stone him. As sojourner, so native, when he blasphemes/pierces the Name, he shall be put to death.

familiar.text: And he that blasphemeth the name of the LORD, he shall surely be put to death, and all the congregation shall certainly stone him: as well the stranger, as he that is born in the land, when he blasphemeth the name of the Lord, shall be put to death.

verses.restored: A man who strikes any human soul/life shall surely be put to death.

familiar.text: And he that killeth any man shall surely be put to death.

verses.restored: One who strikes soul/life of beast shall repay it, soul/life for soul/life.

familiar.text: And he that killeth a beast shall make it good; beast for beast.

familiar.text: Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again.

familiar.text: And he that killeth a beast, he shall restore it: and he that killeth a man, he shall be put to death.

verses.restored: One judgment shall be for you; as sojourner, so native shall it be, for I am YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: Ye shall have one manner of law, as well for the stranger, as for one of your own country: for I am the LORD your God.

verses.restored: Moses spoke to children of Israel, and they brought the one who cursed outside camp and stoned him with stones. Children of Israel did as YHWH commanded Moses.

familiar.text: And Moses spake to the children of Israel, that they should bring forth him that had cursed out of the camp, and stone him with stones. And the children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.

translation_notes: Continual lamp and weekly bread of presence frame the chapter with sustained light, covenant, and holy provision.
The blasphemy verb may carry senses of curse/pierce/name; preserve uncertainty for lexical audit.
The accused is held under guard until judgment is sought, showing process rather than immediate mob action.
Equal-law principle applies to native and sojourner in both the blasphemy case and general judgment.
Eye-for-eye language functions as proportional limitation in ancient law, not permission for escalating revenge; later legal traditions often convert such injury formulas into compensation.
safety_note: Do not use Leviticus 24 to justify blasphemy laws, vigilantism, mob violence, religious persecution, or literal retaliatory mutilation today. The restored layer preserves severe ancient covenant law; interpretation must emphasize due process, equal law, proportional restraint, restitution, and rejection of modern violence.
